supersedes.status: withdrawn after independent review (two blockers, eight majors)

scales.eci_public: Epoch Capabilities Index, public, Bayesian fit of November 2026 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130, GPT-5 = 150). Modelling scale.
scales.aeci_own_card: AECI as printed in the model's own system card. Modelled directly; judgement-heavy. This is what is graded.
scales.aeci_nov6: AECI on the November 6 2026 fit, through a level mapping from public ECI. Secondary.

metadata.interval_convention: median with central 50%, 80% and 95% intervals (lo50/hi50, lo80/hi80, lo95/hi95); null where undefined
caveats: Small samples: 25 Claude models with a public ECI, 21 within-family steps, 8 own-card AECI values, 13 models linking AECI to ECI.
The next-model point forecast is, in effect, 'predecessor + recent record-line slope x elapsed time'. Nothing more elaborate tested better.
Backtest evidence stops at six months ahead (4 folds; 3 with the date unknown, all under-predictions). Haiku's forecast is beyond it.
All backtest folds lie in 2024-26, one regime of rising pace. Every method under-predicted in it.
Beyond about 1.5 years the bands are a scenario projection driven by stated priors, not a validated forecast.
Above public ECI ~208 today's benchmark basket no longer identifies the scale; values there are flagged, not meaningful measurements.
Both indices are re-estimated on every update. AECI rests on first-party internal benchmarks; own-card predictions are judgement with a wide band.
Benchmark predictions are anchored on each family's last score; families near a ceiling get a saturation statement instead.
Release dates come from the site's release forecaster; its errors pass straight through.
The model cannot see regime changes it has no data on (new architectures, export controls, a compute shock, a pause).

notes: AECI own-card values are judgement-heavy estimates.
After validated_through the frontier rows are a scenario projection, not a tested forecast.

scale.rule: Public ECI at which the second-hardest discriminating benchmark (slope >= 0.04) in Epoch's current basket is 90% solved (difficulty + 2.2/slope from Epoch's item parameters). Above it at most one benchmark still separates models, so ECI values are extrapolations of the scale itself, not measurements. Bands above this line are kept in the data and flagged; the page should shade them and need not draw above display_cap_eci.

trend.note: Record-setting releases since Claude 3 Opus (March 2024). 'hinge' = piecewise linear with unknown changepoint; 'jump' = constant slope with a one-time level shift. BIC weights compare four forms on the published point estimates.

all_lab.note: Fitted to all-lab records; no step-up is found, so 'pre-break' pace equals the recent pace and the 'reversion' scenario coincides with 'hold' for this series.

level_process.bootstrap: Subsample bootstrap: each replicate keeps the distinct members of a with-replacement resample of models (about 63%) and one of Epoch's 500 joint posterior draws; record sets are recomputed per replicate. Slope draws outside 4-60 (recent) or 4-40 (pre-break) ECI/yr are clipped to the bound; the share is reported.
level_process.like_for_like: The total slope ratio above (recent / pre-break, public ECI, Anthropic) is the quantity comparable to METR's 1.9x and the card's 1.88x, which are total-slope ratios on AECI. The algorithmic multiplier m used inside the scenarios is a different quantity (it excludes the compute term) and is larger.

gain_model.note: Next = predecessor + max(line gain, 0.3) x exp(c + s z) + measurement noise. The latent step is positive by construction (0 of 21 historical within-family steps were negative); the published score can still fall below the predecessor through measurement noise alone.

families.offsets_note: Offsets from the record line (pooled across families by empirical Bayes) are used only for the family paths after 2027; the next-model forecast uses the gain model. A 'record line + pooled offset' predictor was tested on all folds and is not better (see variants in the release backtest).
families.twin: Fable and Mythos are one underlying model. They are forecast as one entity, 'fable_mythos': one release-date distribution (the forecaster's Fable distribution), one ability draw, one set of benchmark predictions. Public ECI attaches to the Fable label, AECI to the Mythos label.

aeci.primary_scale: Public ECI is the modelling scale (256 models, four years, posterior draws, refittable inputs). AECI is reported two ways: (1) 'own card', the value Anthropic will print in the model's own system card, which is what gets graded and is modelled directly; (2) the November 6 2026 scale, secondary, through a mapping.

own_card.method:
gap_i = own-card AECI_i - public ECI_i (today's Epoch fit; vintage ECI is not available),
one per card that printed an own value, in card order. The gap is a property of the
card's fit (it rose from about -4 to about +4 between May and November 2026, with two
large steps that coincided with basket changes), not of the model's level, so it is
forecast as a level: the mean of the last three cards' gaps. The predictive sd is the
larger of the rolling out-of-sample RMSE of that rule and the sd of the last four gaps,
widened by sqrt(1 + 0.25 (K-1)) for K card refits before the model's own card. Steps are
not treated as iid and no upward drift is extrapolated. Eight cards: a judgement-heavy
estimate, not a tested forecast.
own_card.label: Judgement-heavy estimate with a wide band. The rolling test (five cards) has RMSE 4.3 AECI points; the Haiku 5.5 card missed by 7.6.
own_card.conditional: Sonnet and Haiku own-card predictions are conditional on Anthropic printing one: the Sonnet 5 card printed no AECI. They expire unresolved if the card has none.

caveats: The gap between AECI and public ECI tracks how recent the model and the fit are, not the model's level: Haiku 5.5 (ECI 160.4) printed 167.11 in its own card. A mapping in level alone under-states Sonnet- and Haiku-tier AECI by roughly 2-4 points; the residual sd is set from leave-one-out and held-out errors to cover that.
The level-shift threshold is not identified between ECI 156.3 and 164.1 (no model in between).
Thirteen models on one fit. Secondary quantity.

refits.note: Descriptive only in v2 (the own-card forecast no longer sums refit steps). Three of the seven card-to-card transitions are observed for Opus 5.5 alone, read from cards that state no fit; over those three refits combined, the other models moved +3.8 to +4.5 and Opus 5.5 +5.4. The two large steps coincide with basket changes, so steps are not exchangeable draws.

links.method: Bounded scores follow p = (score - floor)/(ceiling - floor) = sigmoid(a (ability - D)); the ceiling is estimated (with a bootstrap interval) wherever at least four scores lie above 75% of the nominal range, otherwise the nominal ceiling is kept. Predictions are ANCHORED: the family's own last score, moved along the link by the predicted ability gain (on the logit scale for bounded scores, under a ceiling drawn from its bootstrap and never below the last score), plus step noise estimated from past within-family steps. A benchmark is published only if it is not stale (a model scored in the last six months), not saturated (best score below 90% of the ceiling), not too thin, and the anchored method is no worse than 'previous in family' in backtest.

scenarios.definition: Below pre-break pace. Training-compute growth follows the 'low' driver path (2.5x, 2x, 1.5x, 1.5x per year 2027-30) and the algorithmic multiplier falls to 0.4-0.9 of its pre-break value within a year.

The 2025-26 step-up was one-off. Pace returns within six months to 0.85-1.15x the pre-break slope (centred on it, so about half these paths run below pre-break pace), then follows the 'central' compute path down.
The recent trend holds: the algorithmic multiplier stays where the recent slope puts it; compute follows the 'central' driver path (5x, 4x, 3x, 2.5x).
AI R&D feedback: the algorithmic multiplier doubles every 6-12 months until it reaches 4-7.5x, then stays; 60-100% of the excess over 'hold' is realised; compute on the 'central' or 'high' path.
Bounded explosive tail: the multiplier doubles every 3-6 months to a peak of 8-30x, holds 1-2 years, then settles at 3-6x; same 60-100% realisation haircut.

projection.weights_are: priors. 'central' is the author's judgement; 'sceptic' and 'accelerationist' bracket it; 'unweighted_evidence_average' is an unweighted average of three unlike data-based numbers, shown for transparency, not an estimate.

evidence_average_detail.warning: Three numbers that span 0.01 to 0.86 are averaged with equal weight; slowdown and explosive are zero only because the sample contains no such episode. Not an estimate.

projection.validation_statement: Up to 2027-12-31 the bands rest on a backtest of this same code (Anthropic frontier: 16 folds at 0.5 yr, 10 at 1.0, 4 at 1.5, from 16 monthly origins in one regime). Beyond it they are a scenario projection driven by the stated priors: read each scenario path separately and treat the mixture as a summary of the prior.

calibration_applied.rule: Mixture bands are stretched about the median by the factor for their horizon (interpolated between 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 years, held flat beyond). Scenario-conditional bands are not stretched.

bias_term.form: beta * min(h, 1.5) ECI points added to every path; not extrapolated past the longest backtested horizon

reconciliation_with_research_note_1.explanation: Research note 1's central path (17, 17, 16, 15 ECI/yr) is the all-lab frontier continuing at Epoch's reasoning-era slope. For the all-lab series that is our 'hold' and 'reversion' scenarios, which land near it. Our medians are higher for three reasons, in order of size: the Anthropic series has a steeper recent slope than the all-lab series, and Anthropic currently holds the frontier; some prior weight sits on accelerating scenarios; and an explicit under-prediction term is carried where it helped out of sample.

external_comparison.quantity: Capability milestones from a takeoff model
external_comparison.why: v1 translated ECI into METR-style hours to compare; that translation extrapolated two orders of magnitude beyond METR's measurements and has been withdrawn. The 'compounding' and 'explosive' scenarios are the nearest analogue.

metr_horizon.statement: No hours series is published. METR's last measurement is 17.4 hours (Claude Mythos Preview, April 2026) and METR calls estimates above 16 hours unreliable; the fitted link (about 4.75 ECI points per doubling) has no model above public ECI 157.8. Every released frontier model since then, and every projected value, lies beyond that range, so any hours figure would be extrapolation. Qualitatively: if the link held, each further 5 ECI points would double the horizon.

machine.design: The projection code itself (level.LevelProcess.paths, central scenario weights) run at monthly historical origins and scored on the running-max public ECI 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 years later. 'bias_corrected' adds beta*h with beta learned only from folds whose target precedes the origin. Calibration factors are learned the same way and applied to the published bands. Folds overlap heavily; origins span 2024-07 to 2026-05, one regime of rising pace. The scenario weights are today's prior, so this is not a test of the weights.

bias.rule: The term beta*min(h, 1.5) is applied with mean = shrunk estimate only where the rolling (out-of-sample) correction lowered MAE; otherwise its mean is 0 and only its uncertainty is carried.
The term beta*min(h, 1.5) is applied with mean = shrunk estimate only where the rolling (out-of-sample) correction lowered MAE; otherwise its mean is 0 and only its uncertainty is carried.

release.design: Folds are (Claude release, lead) for leads of 0, 3 and 6 months; origin = release date minus lead; everything is refitted on models released strictly before the origin. ALL folds are reported, including the first release of a family (Fable 5), which the model places on the record line. 'model' is told the release date; 'model_date_unknown' is given only the family's cadence up to the origin and is the relevant test of the live forecasts at leads above zero. A baseline is scored on every fold where it is defined (n is shown per row).
release.verdict: On all folds the model's point forecast is not distinguishable from 'previous-in-family + trailing-12-month Anthropic record slope x elapsed time' at any lead (every paired interval spans zero, or favours the baseline). That baseline is therefore the core of the model: next = predecessor + recent record-line gain. What the model adds is a predictive distribution with tested coverage, a positive-step constraint, and consistency with the long-range paths. It does clearly beat 'previous model in family', 'family mean step' and the two all-lab trend lines.
release.what_n_supports: Lead 0 (n=21) supports an error of roughly 2.5 ECI points RMSE with the date known. Three months ahead (n=10, 9 with the date unknown) supports 'about the same, perhaps 3'. Six months ahead (n=4, 3 date-unknown) supports nothing firmer than 'errors of 4-6 points happened and every one was an under-prediction'. No fold has a lead beyond six months: the Haiku forecast (median lead about eight months) is outside anything tested.

calibration.rule: Per level, the larger of the two sets' factors; never below 1.

irt_refit_check.design: Own least-squares 2PL refit of Epoch's benchmark-level inputs, refitted at every fold origin on models released on or before that date, mapped to ECI units by a monotone alignment to the published ECI of those same models. The release backtest is rerun with history from the origin's vintage and the target's actual from the release date's vintage. The fit is deterministic; the vintages are stored in data/irt_vintages.csv.gz, which is committed and covered by the input hash (run.py --full rebuilds it; a test recomputes two vintages and compares).
irt_refit_check.v1_bug: In v1 a date-rounding slip excluded the target from its own vintage on a clean cache, which is why the reviewer's clean run found 18 folds instead of 33. Fixed (tolerance on 'on or before'); numbers below are from a clean rebuild.
irt_refit_check.caveat: Scores in Epoch's input file are today's collection; a score measured after the origin for a model released before it cannot be removed (no timestamps).

benchmarks.design: Same folds as the release backtest (families with an earlier score on the benchmark). 'anchored' is the published method; 'curve_level' is v1's method (the fitted curve's level at the predicted ability), kept for comparison; baseline: the previous model in the family.

review.title: Headline backtest omitted the worst fold; strawman baselines
review.action: Every table is on all folds (Fable 5 included; a first-of-family release is placed on the record line). The reviewer's baseline is a named baseline with paired differences and bootstrap intervals. 'Beats every baseline' is withdrawn: the model is not distinguishable from previous-in-family + trailing-12-month slope, which is now its core.

review.title: Benchmark predictions contradicted observed scores
review.action: Ceilings are estimated where the data allow; predictions are anchored on the family's own last score; saturated, stale and thin benchmarks are dropped with reasons; a family already within a tenth of the ceiling gets a saturation statement instead of a number; tests check every open prediction against observed scores.

review.title: Corner-solution stacking; the two layers disagreed
review.action: Stacking is gone. One level process (equal weights over three recent-trend forms; no all-history forms) feeds both the next-model layer and the projection from the same simulated paths.

review.title: The 2027-30 band was an untested prior
review.action: The projection code is now backtested at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 years on both frontiers, its bias term is estimated out of sample and carried with uncertainty, and its calibration factors are applied. The all-lab frontier is fitted to all-lab data. A below-pre-break scenario exists. Beyond 1.5 years nothing can be tested: those bands remain a prior and are labelled as such; values above the measured scale are flagged.

review.title: Implied METR horizon was false precision
review.action: The hours series and the work-month / work-year probabilities are removed; a qualitative statement replaces them.

review.title: AECI layer
review.action: Own-card AECI is modelled directly from the eight own-card values and labelled a judgement-heavy estimate; refit steps are no longer summed as iid draws; Sonnet/Haiku predictions are marked conditional. It is still eight cards: the rolling test is poor and is reported.

review.title: Twins and grading
review.action: Fable and Mythos are one entity. Unresolvable predictions are pruned; grade.py has an expiry rule and grades against the first published value.

review.title: Regression odds contradicted the record
review.action: Positive-step model; implied P(regression) is reported per entity and is a few percent, from measurement noise only.

review.title: Section 7.4 not reproducible
review.action: Root cause was a date-rounding bug that dropped the target from its own vintage on a clean cache. Fixed; vintages are committed, hashed and tested.

review.title: Live leads untested; calibration a no-op
review.action: The date-unknown variant is the headline for leads above zero and the limits of n are stated. Ability calibration factors are still 1: raw coverage on all folds is at or above nominal, so there is nothing to widen. That is a finding, not an omission; the frontier bands do get non-trivial factors. Haiku's eight-month lead remains untested and is flagged in the output.

review.title: Name-matcher merges
review.action: Dated variants no longer merge into siblings; explicit aliases for Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Oct/Jun); every non-exact match is logged.

review.title: Bootstrap was a subsample; slope draws truncated
review.action: Called a subsample bootstrap; draws are clipped (not discarded) and the clipped share is reported.

review.title: Tests asserted what the code wrote
review.action: Leak tests perturb future data and require unchanged predictions; the mapping test is leave-one-out.

review.title: Monte Carlo noise comparable to differences
review.action: Draws raised; a second-seed rerun is reported; candidate differences inside that noise are no longer interpreted.

review.title: m compared with METR's total-slope ratio
review.action: The total slope ratio is reported for the like-for-like comparison.

review.title: Degenerate frontier floor
review.action: The standing leader's value is drawn from Epoch's posterior.

review.title: Full-sample tuning choices (df, floors, half-life)
review.action: Left as stated assumptions (METHODS section 11). The reviewer measured their effect at RMSE 2.36-2.83, inside fold noise; tuning them by nested cross-validation on ~20 folds would add machinery without changing any number that matters.
